LESSON: ADDITION

Grade: SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade five
Subject: MATHEMATICS
Strand: Numbers
Topic 1.2: Addition
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 6

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Addition, part of Numbers in SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade five MATHEMATICS.

Key inquiry question: How do you estimate the sum of given numbers? 2. How do you create patterns in addition?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. Work out in purposive pairs/groups the sum of three 6 - digit numbers without regrouping up to 1,000 000 using place charts or any other resource. Learners with manipulation difficulties could use alternative functional parts of the body or appropriate assistive technology to work out the sums.

2. Collaborates with others to work out the sum of two 6 - digit numbers with double regrouping with the number not more than 1,000 000 using place value apparatus or any other resource. Learners with speech difficulties could use alternative and augmentative modes of communication (AAC) as they collaborate.

3. Estimate sums by rounding off 1.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. Work out in purposive pairs/groups the sum of three 6 - digit numbers without regrouping up to 1,000 000 using place charts or any other resource. Learners with manipulation difficulties could use alternative functional parts of the body or appropriate assistive technology to work out the sums.
2. Collaborates with others to work out the sum of two 6 - digit numbers with double regrouping with the number not more than 1,000 000 using place value apparatus or any other resource. Learners with speech difficulties could use alternative and augmentative modes of communication (AAC) as they collaborate.
3. Estimate sums by rounding off 1.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Addition together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Values:
Unity: as the learner collaborates with others to work out the sum of two 6 - digit numbers.

Responsibility: Learner enhances responsibility by taking their roles individually to achieve common solutions in addition of

numbers.
